cover.role_line: Temporary Data Operations Analyst · 3 years of service

glance: Your letter offers $8,400 on top of the legal minimum, and it does not give a date to sign by, so ask for any deadline in writing. Some of your details do not match your documents: you told us 3 years of service and $100,000 a year, but your contract is for a temporary role that starts August 11, 2025 and pays by the hour, so the numbers in this report may change once that is sorted out. Your last day was January 30, 2026, which means the 6-month window to file a complaint with the Employment Standards Branch may already have closed. Parts of the contract copy were hard to read, including the signature lines, so a clearer, signed copy would help.
confirmed_line: Built on the details you confirmed on November 5, 2026. Rules as of October 25, 2026.

checks.letter_says: A gross lump sum of $8,400, less withholdings, described as additional to the legal minimum.
checks.rule_says: Unless a valid clause limits you, common-law notice applies. Our estimate is $22,500 to $30,000 (3 to 4 months of base pay).
checks.why: The offer is below our estimate, but the estimate uses 3 years and $100,000 a year, which your contract does not seem to match, so a lawyer can say what range really fits you.

checks.topic: Legal minimum (compensation for length of service)
checks.letter_says: No number of weeks is written.
checks.contract_says: Section 7 refers to amounts required by law.
checks.rule_says: Employment Standards Act: 3 weeks after 3 years of service, which is $5,769 at $1,923 a week of regular wages. British Columbia has no separate severance pay on top of this.
checks.why: This uses 3 years of service. Your contract start date would mean less service, and the Act gives 1 week after 3 months and 2 weeks after 12 months.

checks.rule_says: Notice you already worked comes off the notice still owed.
checks.why: Employment Standards Act notice 3 weeks − 0 weeks you worked = 3 weeks still owed as pay.

checks.rule_says: You need 3 months in a row of work before any compensation for length of service is owed. After that, the weeks grow with your years.
checks.why: You told us 3 years, but the contract start date points to much less. Earlier work for the same employer may count, so ask HR for your start date in writing.

checks.rule_says: The minimum is based on regular wages (base pay).
checks.why: This report uses the $100,000 a year you gave us. Your contract lists an hourly rate that looks lower, so check your pay stubs to see which is right.

checks.rule_says: A bonus counts toward the common-law range only if it was paid most years. It never adds to the legal minimum.
checks.why: In your answers you said you get a bonus, but you confirmed no bonus amount from the contract, so the range here uses base pay only.

checks.topic: Clause limiting you to the minimum
checks.contract_says: No clause limits you to the legal minimum. Section 7 refers to amounts required by law and to common-law obligations.
checks.rule_says: Common-law notice applies unless a valid clause caps you.
checks.why: You confirmed the contract has no clause that limits you to the legal minimum.

checks.rule_says: Not covered by the rules in this report.
checks.why: Your contract calls the job temporary. Whether it had a fixed end date can change what you are owed, and a lawyer can explain how.

checks.letter_says: The extra payment depends on signing a separate severance agreement, which may include a release of claims.
checks.rule_says: Not covered by the rules in this report.
checks.why: The separate agreement was not included, so it is not clear what you would give up by signing it.

checks.letter_says: No end date is written. Benefits follow the plan documents, and the end date will be sent separately.
checks.rule_says: Not covered by the rules in this report.
checks.why: Without an end date, it is not clear how long your coverage lasts.

checks.rule_says: A deadline printed on an offer is the employer's, not the law's. You can ask for more time in writing.
checks.why: Ask HR in writing whether the offer is still open and whether there is a date to respond by.

checks.rule_says: You have 6 months after your last day to file a complaint with the Employment Standards Branch. Missing it does not end a court claim, but it ends the free route.
checks.why: Six months from January 30, 2026 ends around the end of July 2026, so a lawyer can tell you which routes are still open.

checks.rule_says: Apply for EI the week you stop working. Until October 9, 2027, a temporary measure means separation pay does not delay EI.
checks.why: If you have not applied yet, ask Service Canada how a late application is handled.

reasons.service: You told us 3 years, which is a short time. Your contract suggests even less, which would lower this further.
reasons.age: At 23, age usually does not add much time to a notice period.
reasons.job_level: You described the role as professional, but the contract title is a temporary analyst role, so we placed it in the middle.
reasons.similar_jobs: You said there are many similar jobs nearby, which usually means a shorter notice period.

myths.myth: If an offer is more than the legal minimum, it must be fair.
myths.fact: The Employment Standards Act sets only the floor. Common-law notice applies unless a valid clause caps you, and that can be higher.

myths.myth: In British Columbia you get severance pay on top of notice.
myths.fact: The Act has no separate severance layer. Compensation for length of service, up to 8 weeks, is the whole legal floor.

myths.myth: Taking a severance payment delays EI.
myths.fact: Until October 9, 2027, a temporary measure means separation pay is not taken off EI, and the waiting period is waived.

myths.myth: A layoff always means you can be called back later, so nothing is owed.
myths.fact: In British Columbia, a temporary layoff becomes a termination after 13 weeks in any 20-week period. Your letter gives a last scheduled working day.

myths.myth: Missing the 6-month complaint window ends every claim.
myths.fact: It ends the free Employment Standards Branch route, but it does not end a court claim.

clauses.title: Payment depends on a separate agreement
clauses.what_it_says: "conditional on the parties signing a separate written severance agreement that sets out its complete terms, including any release of claims"
clauses.what_it_means: The $8,400 is paid only if you sign another agreement. That agreement may ask you to give up future claims against the employer. It was not included with your letter.
clauses.question_to_ask: What would I give up by signing the release, and how long do I have to review it or change my mind?

clauses.title: What happens when the job ends (contract section 7)
clauses.what_it_says: "any notice, compensation, wages and other amounts required by applicable law and any enforceable contractual or common-law obligations"
clauses.what_it_means: This wording does not limit you to the legal minimum. It refers to both the law and common-law obligations.
clauses.question_to_ask: Since my contract calls the job temporary, does this wording still give me common-law notice?

clauses.title: Benefits
clauses.what_it_says: "will end or continue according to governing plan documents, the terms of any applicable notice period and applicable law"
clauses.what_it_means: No end date is given. The date depends on the plan documents, which the letter says will be sent separately.
clauses.question_to_ask: What date will my benefits end, and can I see the plan documents?

questions: Could you send me a copy of the separate severance agreement, including the release, so I can review it?
Is the offer still open, and is there a date by which I need to respond? Could you confirm that in writing?
What date did my employment start, and does any earlier work for you count toward my years of service?
Was my job a fixed-term contract, and if so, what end date did it have?
What regular wages are you using to work out my compensation for length of service?
How many weeks of compensation for length of service will I receive under the Employment Standards Act, and when will it be paid?
Was I eligible for a bonus, and will any bonus be paid?
What date will my benefits end?
Will vacation pay be added to my compensation for length of service?
Does the severance agreement include a review period or a period to change my mind after signing?
Could you send me a clear, signed copy of my employment contract?
next_steps: Ask HR in writing for the separate severance agreement, a clear signed copy of your contract, and any date to respond by.
Gather your pay stubs, tax slips and any earlier contracts. These will show your real start date and pay.
Wait to sign anything until you have read the full severance agreement and release.
If you have not applied for EI yet, apply now, and ask Service Canada how a late application is handled.
Book a talk with a lawyer about the temporary job title, which routes are still open given the complaint window, and what range fits your real service and pay.
